title: 2003 AMC 10B Problem 16
statement: A restaurant offers three desserts, and exactly twice as many appetizers as main courses. A dinner consists of an appetizer, a main course, and a dessert. What is the least number of main courses that the restaurant should offer so that a customer could have a different dinner each night in the year \(2003?\)

solutions.text:
With \(m\) main courses, the number of dinners is \(3 \cdot m \cdot 2m = 6m^2.\) This must be at least \(365.\)

So \(m^2 \ge \dfrac{365}{6}\approx 60.8.\) Since \(7^2=49\) is too small but \(8^2=64\) works, \(m=8.\)

Thus, the correct answer is E.
hints: With \(m\) main courses there are \(2m\) appetizers, giving \(3 \cdot m \cdot 2m\) dinners
The year \(2003\) is not a leap year, so require \(6m^2 \ge 365\)
